chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a contracted slave who was killed. He said: 'What portion of him was freed is calculated, so the wergild of the free man is paid, and what portion of him remained enslaved is the ransom of the slave.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title primarily referring to Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْحُرِّ: The blood money or compensation paid for killing a free person.
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْعَبْدِ: The blood money or compensation paid for killing a slave.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a certain sum for his freedom.

ai.seo_question: How is the blood money calculated for a partially freed slave who is killed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the proportional calculation of blood money for a mukatab, distinguishing between the portion already emancipated and the portion still enslaved. This ruling, attributed to Imam Ali (AS), highlights the unique legal status of the mukatab as partially free, ensuring that compensation reflects their dual nature. It underscores the principle of equity in Islamic jurisprudence by adjusting financial liabilities according to the degree of freedom retained.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a contracted slave who was killed. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be counted what (proportion) he was free from it, so he (the killer) would pay the wergild of the free, and what (proportion) he was still enslaved from it, is a ransom of the slave’.
